# filmopen_mcp

*Generated by `scripts/package_digest.py`; regenerate, never edit.*

The MCP server for FilmOpen (`docs/archive/FilmOpen-MCP-Plan.md` §3.5). It is a Dart command-line program that an agent's MCP client spawns, and it drives a running FilmOpen agent build through Flutter's driver extension. The MCP library (`dart_mcp`) lives here and nowhere in the app.

**Flutter.** 6 files, 1,898 lines under `lib/`; 68 tests in 5 files. Barrel: `lib/filmopen_mcp.dart`.

## Depends on

- **filmopen_automation (dev)** — uses nothing by name the digest could see

Third-party: dart_mcp, stream_channel, vm_service, flutter_driver.

## Used by

No package of FilmOpen.

What the barrel exports, file by file. A name is `class`, `enum`, `mixin`, `extension`, `typedef`, a top-level function or variable; under a class, its public constructors, fields, getters, setters and methods.

### `lib/src/app_link.dart`

- **class `AppLink`** — The server's line to one running FilmOpen (`docs/archive/FilmOpen-MCP-Plan.md` §3.5): the driver extension's data channel, the whole view as Flutter rendered it, and the wait for an idle frame.
  - `Future<String> requestData(String message)` — Sends one message on the data channel and answers the app's reply.
  - `Future<Uint8List> screenshot()` — A PNG of the app's whole view as Flutter rendered it: every route, dialogs included, but neither the native window frame nor a native dialog.
  - `Future<void> waitIdle()` — Waits until the app has no animation running.
  - `Future<void> enterText(String text)` — Types [text] into the box that has the focus, replacing what it holds, through the driver's own text entry — for the boxes that are not a `FieldRegistry` form: a dialog's (New project, the label, the JSON editor) and…
  - `Future<void> close()` — Closes the connection; the app goes on running.
- **variable** `const String kDriverExtension` — The name the driver extension answers to in an agent build's isolate.
- **class `DriverLink`** — The [AppLink] of a running agent build: Flutter's own driver, handed a connection this link made itself.
  - `DriverLink(this._driver, {this.requestTimeout = const Duration(seconds: 45)})`
  - `static Future<DriverLink> connect(String vmServiceUrl, { Duration timeout = const Duration(seconds: 10), Duration requestTimeout = const Duration(s…` — Connects to the agent build whose VM service answers at [vmServiceUrl].
  - `final Duration requestTimeout` — The longest a request waits for its reply.
- **function** `bool isLocalServiceUrl(String url)` — Whether [url] is a VM service URL on this machine: `http` on the loopback, the only place an app's service listens (§3.6).
- **function** `String redactServiceUrls(String text)` — [text] with the token of every VM service URL in it cut out, the host and the port kept: the token opens the service to whoever holds it (§3.6).
- **class `ServiceUnreachable`** — What a connection meets when nothing answers at a VM service URL: no app, or an app that has gone.
  - `const ServiceUnreachable()`
- **class `NotAnAgentBuild`** — What a connection meets when a service answers but none of its isolates carries the driver extension: an app run without `-t test_driver/agent_main.dart`.
  - `const NotAnAgentBuild()`
- **function** `Uri serviceWebSocketUri(String vmServiceUrl)` — The WebSocket address of a VM service URL, as the driver derives it (`vmservice_driver.dart`): the URL's first path segment, its token, then `ws`.
- **function** `Future<void> probeService(String vmServiceUrl, {Duration timeout = const Duration(seconds: 5)})` — Opens and closes one WebSocket to the VM service at [vmServiceUrl]; throws [ServiceUnreachable] when nothing answers within [timeout].
- **function** `Future<bool> serviceGone(String vmServiceUrl, {Duration timeout = const Duration(seconds: 30)})` — Waits until the VM service at [vmServiceUrl] stops answering, probing every half second for at most [timeout]; answers whether it stopped.

### `lib/src/cli.dart`

- **class `CliCommand`** — One run of the executable (`bin/filmopen_mcp.dart`), read from the words after its options (`docs/archive/FilmOpen-MCP-Plan.md` §3.5): a shell or a script drives an agent build with these, no MCP client needed.
  - `const CliCommand()`
- **class `ServeCommand`** — `serve`, and no words at all: MCP over stdio.
  - `const ServeCommand()`
- **class `OpCommand`** — One message on the data channel: an op, or the literal `ping`.
  - `const OpCommand(this.message, {this.output})`
  - `final String message`
  - `final String? output`
- **class `WindowShotCommand`** — `screenshot [file]`: the whole view as Flutter rendered it, dialogs included.
  - `const WindowShotCommand(this.output)`
  - `final String output`
- **class `WaitIdleCommand`** — `wait-idle`.
  - `const WaitIdleCommand()`
- **class `EnterTextCommand`** — `enter-text <text>`: the driver's own text entry into the box that has the focus — a dialog's, tapped first — replacing what it holds.
  - `const EnterTextCommand(this.text)`
  - `final String text`
- **class `LaunchCommand`** — `launch [platform] [--size WxH] [--home folder]`: `flutter run` in the foreground.
  - `const LaunchCommand(this.platform, {this.size, this.home, this.device})`
  - `final String platform`
  - `final String? size` — `--size <width>x<height>`; null uses the runners' 1280×720.
  - `final String? home` — `--home <folder>` on Linux: the launched app's XDG root.
  - `final String? device` — `--device <serial>` on android, which `adb devices` names; the emulator is `emulator-5554` (milestone 5.01, step 4).
- **class `StopCommand`** — `stop`: asks the agent build to quit through its own channel, and waits for it to end.
  - `const StopCommand()`
- **class `CliUsageError`** — A command line the executable does not understand; [message] says why.
  - `const CliUsageError(this.message)`
  - `final String message`
- **class `CliInvocation`** — A whole command line: the executable's own options and the command.
  - `const CliInvocation({required this.command, this.vmServiceUrl, this.repository, this.help = false})`
  - `final CliCommand command`
  - `final String? vmServiceUrl` — `--vm-service-url`: the agent build to drive.
  - `final String? repository` — `--repo`: the repository `launch` runs in.
  - `final bool help` — `-h`, `--help`.
- **variable** `const String kCliUsage` — The commands, the options and what each takes, for the usage text.
- **function** `CliInvocation parseArguments(List<String> arguments, {required String hostPlatform})` — Reads the whole command line: the executable's own options wherever they stand before a `--`, and every other word as the command's ([parseCommand]), so a command keeps its own `--label`, `--sample` or `-5`.
- **function** `CliCommand parseCommand(List<String> words, {required String hostPlatform})` — Reads [words], the command line without its options; [hostPlatform] is what `launch` runs on when it names none.

### `lib/src/discovery.dart`

- **variable** `const String kAgentFileName` — The name of the file an agent build writes into the application's log folder once it runs (`test_driver/agent_main.dart`).
- **function** `String? agentLogDirectory({Map<String, String>? environment, String? operatingSystem})` — The application's log folder, computed from the environment the way `filmopen_platform`'s `app_paths_io.dart` computes it — the server is a command-line program and cannot import a Flutter plugin (§3.5).
- **class `AgentAnnouncement`** — What `agent.json` says about a running agent build: where its VM service answers, its process, and when it started.
  - `const AgentAnnouncement({required this.vmServiceUrl, required this.pid, this.startedAt})`
  - `final String vmServiceUrl`
  - `final int pid` — The process, for a person reading the file; nothing is decided by it.
  - `final String? startedAt`
  - `static AgentAnnouncement? parse(String text)` — Reads the file's text; null for anything that is not an announcement.
- **function** `Future<AgentAnnouncement?> discoverAgent({ String? directory, Future<bool> Function(AgentAnnouncement announcement)? answers, })` — The running agent build announced in [directory] (the log folder by default), or null: no file, a file that is not an announcement, or one whose service no longer answers — left behind by an app that has gone (§3.5).
- **function** `Future<bool> serviceAnswers(AgentAnnouncement announcement)` — Whether the VM service an announcement names answers ([probeService]).
